messages:
maria: :rotating_light: paging on azc egress — customers hitting timeouts to external APIs from instances in azc-private-*/svc-tier. Not all hosts, looks like a subset of subnets.
jon: I see spike in 5xx and connection timeouts to third-party payment gateway. Metric spike started ~10:12 UTC.
nashwin: I'm oncall taking this. @sre-pager can you open an incident and assign to infra?
sre-pager: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-azc-egress. Priority P1. Paging infra and oncall SRE.
nashwin: Thanks. Quick blamestorm — any recent infra changes in azc? terraform plans applied around 09:50 UTC for multi-az NAT cleanup.
infra-bot: deploy-log: terraform apply done by deploy-bot at 09:52 UTC. Changed: aws_route_table_association.private-rt-azc -> associated with subnet-azc-3b, removed old association from subnet-azc-3c.
nate: I can confirm route-table associations were modified. Could be race with a later automated rollback that didn't complete.
jon: Traceroutes from affected hosts: first hop to nat-azc is fine, then traffic drops. curl to 1.1.1.1 hangs after SYN_SENT.
maria: S3 access from same hosts works. So it's not total egress blackhole — selective external hosts failing.
nashwin: Check NAT gateway health and route table entries.
ate: NAT-GW-azc shows healthy, metrics show TX/RX, but CloudTrail shows a ReplaceRoute call at 09:53 that updated 0.0.0.0/0 -> eni-zzz (previously nat-gw-azc). There is an orphaned instance NAT shim we forgot to remove; its source/destination check is enabled.
jon: That would explain asymmetric return path — packets go out via ENI instance, replies drop because the instance isn't doing nat.
nashwin: Can we flip the route back to nat-gw-azc and re-associate correct route table?
ops-lead: Do it carefully — we need rollback steps and to avoid flapping for healthy AZs. Document actions in-channel.
ate: Rolling route update now: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0abcde
```
maria: While that's in flight, I see some hosts still failing. Also noticed NACL on the subnet-azc-3c was modified yesterday to a deny-all ephemeral range? Noted an accidental rule addition: deny TCP 1024-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0.
jon: That would break return traffic for ephemeral ports. Two independent issues — route pointing to ENI and NACL blocking ephemeral replies.
nate: Route replacement completed, route now points to nat-0abcde. Confirming from host: curl to payment gateway now completes for some instances.
nashwin: Great. Now fix NACL. What's the change set?
ate: NACL rule id nacl-xyz had a deny 1024-65535. Removing it now.
ate: Removing rule -> applied.
maria: Re-testing across the fleet — so far 80% recovered, remaining failures tied to hosts that were using the ENI path and have conntrack entries stuck.
jon: Conntrack flush on affected hosts will help. Recommend issuing a rolling restart of the snat service or restart networking.
nashwin: I'll coordinate with oncall to run conntrack -F on affected boxes, will target one subnet at a time. Notify CS.
customer-success: Notifying impacted customers about degraded external calls and mitigation in progress. Messaging: we’ve identified a networking configuration issue affecting some requests from instances in azc; mitigation underway.
ops-lead: Good. Also schedule post-incident: audit terraform state drift and prune any leftover ENIs used as shim.
maria: Post-mortem notes in brief: 1) terraform changed route table assoc but a manual/automation change replaced route target to an instance ENI; 2) accidental NACL deny broke ephemeral ports; 3) conntrack caused stuck flows; 4) cross-AZ fallback NAT wasn't used because route mispointed.
nashwin: Mitigations done: restored route -> nat-gw, removed bad NACL rule, flushed conntrack on affected hosts. Monitoring shows error rates back to baseline.
sre-pager: Incident INC-2026-0423-azc-egress status: mitigated. Will keep open for 2hr watch.
ops-lead: Action items: (a) add terraform pre-apply guard against ENI route targets; (b) prevent NACL broad ephemeral denies in deploy linting; (c) add automated check that 0.0.0.0/0 points to nat-gw if route-table is private-rt; (d) run conntrack cleanup playbook on impacted subnets.
maria: Assigning owners: nate -> terraform guard; jon -> conntrack playbook improvements; ashwin -> run full audit and write postmortem.
nashwin: Oncall handoff in 45m to @ops-lead. Leaving channel once watch period passed.
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
